result.summary: The street features sidewalks on both sides and a dedicated bike lane, but the environment is dominated by an elevated rail structure that creates significant visual obstructions and shadows. There are no marked pedestrian crossings visible within the block, and the presence of parked vehicles further limits sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Infrastructure
hazards.description: The large support pillars for the elevated rail structure create significant blind spots for both drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and right side of the roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks are visible, which may lead to unpredictable mid-block crossing behavior in a commercial area.

hazards.name: Poor Visibility due to Shadows
hazards.description: The overhead structure creates deep shadows that can obscure pedestrians from drivers' view even during daylight.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway and sidewalks under the elevated tracks

interventions.title: High-Visibility Mid-block Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a marked crossing with high-visibility paint and signage to provide a predictable location for pedestrians to cross.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight beyond the parked cars and pillars.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lighting specifically directed at the sidewalk and crossing areas to counteract the shadows cast by the elevated rail structure.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is located under an elevated transit structure, which introduces significant visual and physical obstructions due to large support pillars. While a continuous sidewalk and on-street parking buffer are present, the environment suffers from poor natural light and a lack of mid-block crossing infrastructure.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is defined by an elevated rail structure that creates a dark, shadowed corridor with significant visual obstructions from support columns. While continuous sidewalks and parallel parking provide basic infrastructure, the lack of marked crossings and the presence of physical obstacles on the walkway limit safety and accessibility.

hazards.name: Elevated rail columns
hazards.description: Large steel columns located on or near the sidewalk create pinch points for pedestrians and block sightlines between drivers and people on the walkway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the roadway supporting the overhead structure

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: No visible crosswalks are provided in this stretch, requiring pedestrians to cross the street without designated protection or markings.

hazards.name: Parked vehicle sightline obstruction
hazards.description: Parallel parked cars along the curb can obscure pedestrians, particularly children, from the view of approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add zebra-style marked crossings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and alert drivers to crossing locations.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Supplement existing street lighting with fixtures directed at the sidewalk to improve visibility under the dark elevated structure.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is significantly constrained by large structural pillars for an elevated railway that occupy the center of the sidewalk. These pillars create narrow pinch points and obstruct visibility between pedestrians and motorists on a street with active commercial frontages.

hazards.name: Elevated Railway Pillar
hazards.description: A large steel pillar supporting the elevated train tracks is positioned in the middle of the sidewalk, creating a significant physical obstruction and narrowing the effective walking path.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the sidewalk, vertically spanning the frame.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb line create a visual barrier that prevents pedestrians and drivers from seeing each other clearly.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb on the left and right sides of the foreground.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions (bulb-outs) to widen the sidewalk area around the structural pillars, increasing the effective walking width and improving visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install lighting fixtures specifically aimed at the sidewalk under the elevated structure to improve visibility and safety during low-light conditions.
